figures.caption: Figure 2: Task accuracy (%, ↑) and privacy score (%, ↑) under the base system prompt, four defense variants, and jointly optimized system prompt. Stronger privacy directives shift models toward higher privacy score but lower task accuracy, tracing a consistent trade-off curve that no hand-crafted variant escapes.
Table 4: Private fields per document type.

Table 2: Per-model difference in Task (%, ↑) and privacy score (%, ↑) between authorized and unauthorized access conditions (∆ = Auth−Unauth), evaluated on corporate document types. Green (+) indicates auth outperforms unauth; red (−) indicates auth underperforms unauth. A negative ∆Priv (red) means the model leaks more when told the user is authorized, revealing susceptibility to authorization-based social engineering.

Figure 3: Change in privacy score (∆Privacy = PrivacyVariant − PrivacyDirect) for each attack variant (Ignore, Important, Roleplay) relative to the Direct baseline. Positive ∆ indicates that the adversarial phrasing raises privacy score, i.e., the model treats attack language as an alarm signal. Proprietary models (left 4) dominate the positive-∆ region, while open-source models generally show smaller ∆.

Figure 6: Dataset statistics of TRAP. (a) Document type and modality distribution across 500 samples (50 per type). (b) Number of unique tools and private/non-private fields per document type. (c) Distribution of required tool arguments per sample, broken down by document type (min–max range with mean).
Table 3: Sample distribution by document type and modality.

Figure 1: Overview of TRAP. Given multimodal documents and a tool list, a model is evaluated on two queries: a task query requiring correct tool invocation with private field values, and an attack query attempting to elicit the same information in natural language. The two possible outcomes illustrate the core trade-off, implying that task success and privacy protection are not independent.

Figure 7: Examples of private field masking. Masked regions are replaced with a private key (shown as [PRIVATE_*]). Image examples show pixel-level redaction; text examples show inline token substitution.

Table 1: Evaluation of model vulnerability. Task (%, ↑) measures tool + argument correctness. Privacy (%, ↑) is 1− leakage rate. HM (↑) is the harmonic mean of Overall Task and Privacy. Overall Task is shaded green (darker = higher), Privacy red (darker = lower, i.e. worse), and HM purple (darker = higher).
